history.dynasty: Modern — commissioned by Aashiyaan Estate Developers; creator listed as Shree Shivananda Sinha (per Wikipedia)
history.period: Construction began July 2010; opened to the public 14 July 2012
history.summary: A modern Shakta temple at Kalika Vihar, Aashiyan Garden Phase-3, Chira Chas, Bokaro — the mini-township of Kalika Vihar is named after it. Built by Aashiyaan Estate Developers in under three years (July 2010 to 14 July 2012; before the foundation a nine-day Ramayana recital and yagna were held), it is a two-storey pentagonal structure over 90 feet tall, designed to imitate a lotus flower with five petals, each petal housing an entrance, and over 160 feet long. The main shrine on the first floor holds a Kali idol in her Sita avatar (one source calls it a 10-foot black-stone idol — verify); a small Hanuman temple stands at the entrance and a large prayer/yagna hall occupies the basement (over 4000 sq ft). Local legend: labourers found an Indian cobra during foundation excavation, taken as a good omen symbolising Shiva; devotees believe the goddess grants wishes. The opening was covered by major Jharkhand newspapers and the temple is now a prominent pilgrimage stop in the state.

name: Sri Sri Kalika Maharani Temple
town_description: Bokaro Steel City is a planned industrial city in Bokaro district, Jharkhand, built around the Bokaro Steel Plant — one of India's first public-sector steel plants, commissioned in the 1960s with Soviet collaboration. The city is laid out in numbered sectors with broad avenues, parks and markets, and draws settlers from across India, which is reflected in its temples representing many regional traditions. Nearby attractions include Garga Dam, the Parasnath Hills (a major Jain pilgrimage site) and the Rajrappa Chhinnamasta temple.

travel.airport: Birsa Munda Airport, Ranchi — about 120 km from Bokaro Steel City (verify).
travel.railway: Bokaro Steel City railway station (BKSC) is the nearest major railhead; the temple at Chira Chas is about 12 km from the Bokaro Steel City centre (per a travel blog — verify).
travel.road: Kalika Vihar, Aashiyan Garden Phase-3, Chira Chas — reachable by road from Bokaro Steel City via Chas; one review notes the approach road was in poor condition at the time (verify current state).
